openspec.differenceExplained: openspec/changes/session-completion-sprints is untracked in main, so it is absent from a worktree created at HEAD. Not a regression.

limits: Offline source implementation only. This does not establish process containment, financial success, Docker execution or Preview acceptance, and grants no admission.

laneDeclaredGaps.summary: No AF_UNIX socket or nonce handshake. The caller uses the documented argv protocol of launch-local.mjs and preview-launch.mjs instead; the socket protocol belongs to a separate executor.
writeControlRecord and readDurableResult are injectable dependencies with no production filesystem default wired this round.

startupValid, evidencePreexists and invocationIdMismatch are passed conservative literal defaults in executor-caller.mjs rather than detected against a real store. fault-matrix.mjs implements and tests those rows independently.
terminalEvidencePersisted and stopReceiptPersisted are conflated: one durable-result read stands in for both.
No hard-wired call to validatePreviewFinancialCompletion or localFinancialCommandExitCode inside executor-caller.mjs; left to a production caller supplying readDurableResult.

The total precedence order across the 14 fault-matrix rows is the implementer’s own choice. The spec states only two ordering rules explicitly. Documented and tested, but another spec-consistent ordering is possible.

correctionRound1.functionalConsequence: PROCESS_SUCCESS is no longer reachable from this caller, because it never durably writes terminal evidence and now reports that honestly instead of supplying an invented zero. This is the spec-correct outcome, and it is a real functional limit to carry forward, not a defect.

openWork.summary: The one-shot runner invocation handoff protocol: AF_UNIX socket and mode bits, 256-bit nonce, env pinning, constant-time comparison, peer UID, /proc PID ancestry, one-handshake rule, pre-handshake durable event, EOF semantics, and the seven denial cases. Not attempted.

The static PID 1 prover-lifetime C wrapper, its reproducible build, and offline tests that compile it and drive children that exit, hang, fork, change process group and ignore signals. No such file exists. The delivered module is a correct pure model of its arithmetic and control-record bytes only.

taskCompletionStatement: Task 5.2 is NOT complete. Of its three scoped spec requirements, the fault matrix and the prover-lifetime arithmetic model are delivered and audited, while the one-shot handoff protocol and the static C wrapper are open. Closing 5.2 requires both.

auditRound2.artifact: AUDIT-OPUS-02.md / .json at the lane worktree root

priorBlockingFindings.F1: fixed, verified by mutation and live probe
priorBlockingFindings.F2: fixed, unreachable success judged spec-correct rather than an overshoot

auditRound2.method: The auditor proved F1 by mutation: collapsing the substitution site fails the retitled test, and hoisting the provenance flag above the guard so a denied kill also launders fails the new denied-kill test. It proved the seven new tests load-bearing by making ten separate reversions on a scratch copy, each of which killed exactly the expected test. It compared the matrix exhaustively across 368,640 inputs.
auditRound2.auditorSelfCorrection: In round one the auditor proposed mapping a caller kill to DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. It now records that the spec assigns MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE to an outer kill without a retained terminal observation, which is tighter than its own earlier suggestion, and that the implementer followed the spec rather than the reviewer. It also explicitly retracted a round-one overstatement.

exhaustiveMatrixComparison.note: The two closed cases are significant: success was previously reachable with no observed main exit.

newFindings.summary: Because terminalEvidencePersisted is unconditionally false, every clean run now reports EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED for a write that was never attempted, which masks a real deadline crossing in one branch.
The new row absorbs STOP_FAILED and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED among 4,606 relabelled classifications, all with unknown raw exit.
The post-kill bound settles the promise but not the process: measured 305ms settle against 4,028ms parent exit, with the child pipes still held and no pid returned for the outstanding cleanup owner.
startupValid is still passed as true unobserved, and is no longer disclosed as such.
The containment validation added for F3 no longer gates anything.

auditRound2.acceptanceDecision: Accepted as a verified increment. The audit approved it, both blocking defects are genuinely fixed, and the orchestrator independently re-ran all seven suites. The six new findings are all low and are recorded as open follow-ups rather than treated as resolved. N1 in particular will mislead a reader and should be fixed before this caller is used in anger.
